itineraries.title: Beautiful British Columbia with Tyne and Michael
itineraries.content:
Tyne and Michael explore “Beautiful British Columbia” (BBC).

![](/travel-files/beautiful-british-columbia-with-tyne-and-michael/000-download.webp)


## Who


![](/travel-files/beautiful-british-columbia-with-tyne-and-michael/001-image.webp)

![](/travel-files/beautiful-british-columbia-with-tyne-and-michael/002-image.webp)


## What


> Hoping to have a new truck by then (can still rent if need be) but it'll defs be not great on gas so thinking maybe we try n stay in the radius of like Kelowna/Kamloops/100 mile house sorta vibe, so maybe a loop up north and then down and along the Choquihalla or smtn like that with a combo of car camping and backpacking (and climbing 👀). We can always go further afield but just guna start gettin real steep on gas if we're gettin into the Rockies and shit


### Packing 🎒


Make sure to charge all electronics.

- General
    - [x] Shirts
    - [x] Jeans
    - [x] Casual shoes
    - [x] Water bottle—Nalgene
    - [x] Backpack
    - [x] Computer (with charger) + crappy mouse
    - [x] Camera (with charger)
    - [x] GoPro (with gear), clear some memory
    - [x] Drone (with gear), test it out
    - [x] Watch (with charger)
    - [x] Battery pack
    - [x] Kindle
    - [x] Bullet journal
    - [x] Empty journal or notebook
    - [ ] Running gear (and also stuff to climb in)
    - [x] Stuff to chill in Vancouver and on road trip (at bars, etc.)
    - [ ] ~~Blundstones, if available~~
    - [ ] Swim suit
- Backpacking gear—avoid cotton
    - [x] Wool or synthetic hiking shirts
    - [x] Wool or synthetic hiking pants
    - [x] Wool hiking socks
    - [x] Rain jacket
    - [x] Rain pants
    - [x] Warm layers (fleeces or puffy jackets if you got them—again, avoid cotton)
    - [x] Baseball cap
    - [ ] Toque
    - [x] Sunglasses
    - [x] Hiking boots
    - [x] Camp shoes (Crocs or sandals)
- Car camping gear
    - [ ] Guns
        - [ ] More guns
    - [ ] Bullets
    - [ ] Fishing rods

Michael’s shopping list: hiking shoes (Merrell Moab 3 Mid or similar), new backpack (Osprey Farpoint or Fairview—daypack and would cover Europe, or similar), rain gear (pants and jacket), hiking pants, packing cubes

Things to procure in Vancouver: more layers, extra socks, more rain gear?


## Where


BBC (”Beautiful British Columbia”).


## Why


It’s nails.


## When


Leave on Aug 28th

Get back on Sept 2nd.


### Day 1


[Keith’s Hut ](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/canada/british-columbia/keiths-hut)

    Drive up north from Vancouver to Pemby ([lunch](https://www.bing.com/alink/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mileoneeatinghouse.com%2F&h=Y%2BvhmFKaXiXkdE38uF3998ANoAzZptQZAkHEt2NqpWg%3D&p=lw_mapsdc&ig=A4D25605A7FD4DD98BDEED9BEABE9DEF&ypid=YN1226x889524103)) → take Duffey Lake road → Hike up to Keith’s Hut (5.67km/2hr from watch, some wrong turns occurred) → post up at Keiths (late start, didn’t do further hikes) 

        Optional Side Quests (not completed): 

            - [Vantage peak](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/canada/british-columbia/vantage-peak) → scrambles but no glacier/climbing gear needed
            - [Joffrey Peak](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/canada/british-columbia/joffre-peak-via-cerise-creek-summer-trail) → hard scrambles, glacier traverse gear needed and probably some climbing kit (repelling?)


### Day 2


Bull Canyon 

    Hike out from Keiths (lost the trail cuz deadfall, bush waking, Mike meets type 2 fun, wasn't actually that bad though) → drive to Lillooet ([lunch](https://www.bing.com/alink/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Fabundancebakery.ca%2F&h=GMC%2F56Kucwa2GU6LRYfWi9TXW2eCOCMGOK5b0G5NajY%3D&p=lw_mapsdc&ig=EA157BDAEE5F479F83DE3C59D668B32F&ypid=YN1226x5870124540215449926)) → 


### Day 2-3


Drive up to the Fraser Plateau; camped at Bowron Lake.


### Day 3-5


Mosey over to Wells Gray park. See some waterfalls; hike Trophy Mountain.


### Day 6


Pit stop in Hope on the way back. Hit up some bars.


### Day 7


Home!

itineraries.title: Vietnam
itineraries.description: Eleven days north to south, from Hanoi and the Ha Giang loop down to Saigon.

waypoints.title: Hanoi
waypoints.notes: Old Quarter walking tour, egg coffee, and Train Street.

waypoints.title: Ha Giang
waypoints.notes: The Ha Giang loop by motorbike, easily the highlight.

waypoints.title: Cat Ba
waypoints.notes: A boat cruise with Cat Ba Ventures; the most chill day of the trip.

waypoints.title: Ninh Binh

waypoints.title: Ho Chi Minh City
waypoints.notes: War Remnants Museum, the Bitexco sky deck, and the Cu Chi tunnels.

itineraries.content:
Eleven days up and down Vietnam over the April break on exchange. It ran north to south, from Hanoi out to the mountains and then down to Saigon.

Hanoi came first: a free walking tour of the Old Quarter, egg coffee, Train Street, and the (muggy) views from the Lotte observation deck. Then the big one, the Ha Giang loop, a few days riding the mountain roads up near the Chinese border. After that an overnight bus to Cat Ba for a boat cruise with Cat Ba Ventures, the most chill day of the trip, and a stop in Ninh Binh for another boat through Trang An plus the Mua Caves in the fog. I flew down to Ho Chi Minh City to finish: Pizza 4P's, the War Remnants Museum, the Bitexco sky deck, a night on Bui Vien, and the Cu Chi tunnels the next morning, before flying home to Singapore.


## Route


- Hanoi (Apr 7–9)
- Ha Giang loop (Apr 10–12)
- Cat Ba (Apr 13)
- Ninh Binh (Apr 14)
- Ho Chi Minh City (Apr 15–16)

itineraries.title: Hong Kong
itineraries.description: Six days of sightseeing wedged between paper deadlines on exchange.

waypoints.title: Hong Kong Island
waypoints.notes: Causeway Bay, the Monster Building, and the Quarry Bay promenade.

waypoints.title: Kowloon
waypoints.notes: A day with a local friend and the Symphony of Lights.

waypoints.title: Lantau Island
waypoints.notes: Ngong Ping 360 up to the Tian Tan Buddha, then the village at Tai O.

itineraries.content:
Six days in Hong Kong over the April break on exchange, mostly working on a paper between sightseeing, with a friend showing me around for part of it.

I was based on Hong Kong Island: Causeway Bay, the Monster Building and the Quarry Bay promenade, the Central-Mid-Levels escalators, and a fair bit of laptop time in cafes and British pubs. One day I spent with my friend Jacky, ending at the horse racing. Over in Kowloon there was the waterfront and the Symphony of Lights. The best day was out on Lantau: the Ngong Ping 360 cable car up to the Tian Tan Buddha and the Wisdom Path, then the old fishing village at Tai O. I flew out late on the last night, landing in Hanoi around 1am to start the next trip.


## Route


- Hong Kong Island (Apr 3–4)
- Kowloon (Apr 5)
- Lantau Island (Apr 6)

itineraries.title: Philippines
itineraries.description: A week of island-hopping and diving through the Visayas.

waypoints.title: Cebu City
waypoints.notes: Landed before dawn and dove around Mactan Island.

waypoints.title: Panglao
waypoints.notes: Bohol's Chocolate Hills and tarsiers, plus diving off Panglao.

waypoints.title: Moalboal
waypoints.notes: The sardine run and Kawasan Falls canyoneering.

itineraries.content:
A week island-hopping the Philippines with a friend, over the March break on exchange. It was mostly built around diving in the Visayas.

We flew into Cebu before dawn and dove around Mactan, then ferried over to Bohol for Chocolate Hills, tarsiers, and a couple of days diving off Panglao. The plan had been to stop in Oslob for the whale sharks on the way south, but the ferry broke down, so we skipped it and pushed on to Moalboal. That turned out fine: the sardine run just off the beach, and canyoneering at Kawasan Falls. From there it was back up to Cebu City for a 3am flight onward to Malaysia.

Palawan and El Nido were on the original plan and didn't survive the final cut; saving those for another lifetime.


## Route


- Cebu / Mactan (Mar 23)
- Bohol / Panglao (Mar 24–26)
- Moalboal (Mar 27–28)

itineraries.title: Thailand
itineraries.description: Temples up in Bangkok, then islands down south; eight days over a break on exchange.

waypoints.title: Bangkok
waypoints.notes: Temples, Khao San Road, and a day trip out to the ruins at Ayutthaya.

waypoints.title: Koh Samui
waypoints.notes: Island time after the overnight train down to Surat Thani.

waypoints.title: Krabi
waypoints.notes: Limestone cliffs around Ao Nang and a Phi Phi day trip.

itineraries.content:
Eight days through Thailand while I was on exchange in Singapore, with a couple of friends joining partway. It split cleanly into temples up north and islands down south.

I started in Bangkok for the big sights: Wat Pho, the Grand Palace and Wat Arun, the Chatuchak weekend market, and a day trip out to the old ruins at Ayutthaya. Evenings went to Khao San Road. From there I took the overnight train down to Surat Thani and crossed to Koh Samui for a couple of slow beach days. The trip finished in Krabi, based in Ao Nang, with a day out to the Phi Phi islands before flying back to Singapore via Kuala Lumpur.


## Route


- Bangkok (Feb 18–20)
- Koh Samui (Feb 21–22)
- Krabi / Ao Nang (Feb 23–25)

itineraries.title: Indonesia
itineraries.description: A week of temples and volcanoes across Java and Bali, on not much sleep.

waypoints.title: Yogyakarta
waypoints.notes: The temples at Borobudur and Prambanan.

waypoints.title: Malang
waypoints.notes: Base for the Tumpak Sewu waterfall.

waypoints.title: Mount Bromo
waypoints.notes: The classic sunrise hike over the caldera.

waypoints.title: Mount Ijen
waypoints.notes: A midnight start for the crater and its blue fire.

waypoints.title: Bali
waypoints.notes: Nusa Penida and Uluwatu to close it out.

itineraries.content:
A week across Java and Bali with a friend, over a reading break on exchange. The pitch was temples and volcanoes, and it delivered on both; not much sleep was involved.

We started in Yogyakarta for the two big temples, Prambanan and Borobudur, then took an overnight train east to Malang to reach the Tumpak Sewu waterfall. From there it was the classic East Java run: a pre-dawn jeep up Mount Bromo for sunrise over the caldera, then a midnight hike up Mount Ijen for the crater and its sulphur fires. We crossed by ferry to Bali to finish, with a day trip to Nusa Penida and sunset at Uluwatu before flying back to Singapore.

It was rainy season the whole way and the early starts were brutal, but the volcanoes made it.


## Route


- Yogyakarta (Feb 3–4)
- Malang / Tumpak Sewu (Feb 5)
- Mount Bromo (Feb 6)
- Mount Ijen (Feb 7)
- Bali (Feb 8–9)

itineraries.title: Malaysia
itineraries.description: Penang and the Cameron Highlands over a Chinese New Year weekend.

waypoints.title: Penang
waypoints.notes: George Town street art, the Monkey Beach hike, and Chinese New Year fireworks.

waypoints.title: Cameron Highlands
waypoints.notes: Tea plantations above Tanah Rata.

itineraries.content:
Malaysia was the easy one to reach from Singapore, just over the causeway, so I ended up going a few times. This was the big loop, over the Chinese New Year long weekend in January.

I crossed through Johor and took an overnight bus up to Penang. George Town is the draw: street art, hawker food in Little India, the Kek Lok Si temple, and a hike out to Monkey Beach in the national park. I caught the Chinese New Year fireworks there. From Penang I headed inland and up to the Cameron Highlands, where the afternoon went to a tea plantation above Tanah Rata.

My notes for the back half of this trip never got written up, so I'll leave it there; Kuala Lumpur and Melaka were on the list and are worth their own visit.


## Route


- Penang / George Town (Jan 21)
- Cameron Highlands (Jan 22)

South East Asia.description: Eleven days north to south, from Hanoi and the Ha Giang loop down to Saigon.

waypoints.title: Ninh Binh
waypoints.notes: Trang An boat cruise and the Mua Caves, fog and all.

waypoints.title: Ho Chi Minh City
waypoints.notes: War Remnants Museum, the Bitexco sky deck, and the Cu Chi tunnels.

South East Asia.content:
Eleven days up and down Vietnam over the April break on exchange. It ran north to south, from Hanoi out to the mountains and then down to Saigon.

Hanoi came first: a free walking tour of the Old Quarter, egg coffee, Train Street, and the (muggy) views from the Lotte observation deck. Then the big one, the Ha Giang loop, a few days riding the mountain roads up near the Chinese border. After that an overnight bus to Cat Ba for a boat cruise with Cat Ba Ventures, the most chill day of the trip, and a stop in Ninh Binh for another boat through Trang An plus the Mua Caves in the fog. I flew down to Ho Chi Minh City to finish: Pizza 4P's, the War Remnants Museum, the Bitexco sky deck, a night on Bui Vien, and the Cu Chi tunnels the next morning, before flying home to Singapore.


## Route


- Hanoi (Apr 7–9)
- Ha Giang loop (Apr 10–12)
- Cat Ba (Apr 13)
- Ninh Binh (Apr 14)
- Ho Chi Minh City (Apr 15–16)

South East Asia.content:
A week island-hopping the Philippines with a friend, over the March break on exchange. It was mostly built around diving in the Visayas.

We flew into Cebu before dawn and dove around Mactan, then ferried over to Bohol for Chocolate Hills, tarsiers, and a couple of days diving off Panglao. The plan had been to stop in Oslob for the whale sharks on the way south, but the ferry broke down, so we skipped it and pushed on to Moalboal. That turned out fine: the sardine run just off the beach, and canyoneering at Kawasan Falls. From there it was back up to Cebu City for a 3am flight onward to Malaysia.

Palawan and El Nido were on the original plan and didn't survive the final cut; saving those for another lifetime.


## Route


- Cebu / Mactan (Mar 23)
- Bohol / Panglao (Mar 24–26)
- Moalboal (Mar 27–28)

South East Asia.content:
Eight days through Thailand while I was on exchange in Singapore, with a couple of friends joining partway. It split cleanly into temples up north and islands down south.

I started in Bangkok for the big sights: Wat Pho, the Grand Palace and Wat Arun, the Chatuchak weekend market, and a day trip out to the old ruins at Ayutthaya. Evenings went to Khao San Road. From there I took the overnight train down to Surat Thani and crossed to Koh Samui for a couple of slow beach days. The trip finished in Krabi, based in Ao Nang, with a day out to the Phi Phi islands before flying back to Singapore via Kuala Lumpur.

- Bangkok (Feb 18–20)
- Koh Samui (Feb 21–22)
- Krabi / Ao Nang (Feb 23–25)

South East Asia.description: A week of temples and volcanoes across Java and Bali, on not much sleep.

South East Asia.content:
A week across Java and Bali with a friend, over a reading break on exchange. The pitch was temples and volcanoes, and it delivered on both; not much sleep was involved.

We started in Yogyakarta for the two big temples, Prambanan and Borobudur, then took an overnight train east to Malang to reach the Tumpak Sewu waterfall. From there it was the classic East Java run: a pre-dawn jeep up Mount Bromo for sunrise over the caldera, then a midnight hike up Mount Ijen for the crater and its sulphur fires. We crossed by ferry to Bali to finish, with a day trip to Nusa Penida and sunset at Uluwatu before flying back to Singapore.

It was rainy season the whole way and the early starts were brutal, but the volcanoes made it.

waypoints.title: Cameron Highlands

South East Asia.content:
Malaysia was the easy one to reach from Singapore, just over the causeway, so I ended up going a few times. This was the big loop, over the Chinese New Year long weekend in January.

I crossed through Johor and took an overnight bus up to Penang. George Town is the draw: street art, hawker food in Little India, the Kek Lok Si temple, and a hike out to Monkey Beach in the national park. I caught the Chinese New Year fireworks there. From Penang I headed inland and up to the Cameron Highlands, where the afternoon went to a tea plantation above Tanah Rata.

My notes for the back half of this trip never got written up, so I'll leave it there; Kuala Lumpur and Melaka were on the list and are worth their own visit.


## Route


- Penang / George Town (Jan 21)
- Cameron Highlands (Jan 22)

waypoints.notes: Ngong Ping 360 up to the Tian Tan Buddha, then the village at Tai O.

East Asia.content:
Six days in Hong Kong over the April break on exchange, mostly working on a paper between sightseeing, with a friend showing me around for part of it.

I was based on Hong Kong Island: Causeway Bay, the Monster Building and the Quarry Bay promenade, the Central-Mid-Levels escalators, and a fair bit of laptop time in cafes and British pubs. One day I spent with my friend Jacky, ending at the horse racing. Over in Kowloon there was the waterfront and the Symphony of Lights. The best day was out on Lantau: the Ngong Ping 360 cable car up to the Tian Tan Buddha and the Wisdom Path, then the old fishing village at Tai O. I flew out late on the last night, landing in Hanoi around 1am to start the next trip.


## Route


- Hong Kong Island (Apr 3–4)
- Kowloon (Apr 5)
- Lantau Island (Apr 6)
